description: A striking small bird frequently seen in Lima's parks. The male is bright red with a dark mask and wings, while the female is grayish-brown with a streaked belly.
One of the most common doves in Lima, easily recognizable by its distinctive blue eye-ring, white wing patches, and its melodic 'cu-cu-li' call.
A medium-sized hummingbird found in arid coastal regions. Males have a long, deeply forked tail and a shimmering purple throat patch.
A primarily nocturnal, terrestrial bird with large yellow eyes and long greenish legs. It is often found in open fields, agricultural areas, and arid coastal strips.
A bright yellow finch commonly found foraging on the ground in lawns and parks. Males are vibrant yellow with an orange crown, while females are duller and streaked.
Also known as the Rufous-collared Sparrow, this adaptable bird is found from coastal cities up to the Andes. It has a distinctive rufous collar and a striped head.
